newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 6.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- State prosecutors said Wednesday they will summon two politicans, Kwon Roh-kap and Hong In-gil, for questioning on their possible roles in the Hanbo Group loan scandal as early as next week.
- Prosecutors placed under arrest on Wednesday two heads of local banks, Sheen Kwang-shik and Woo Chan-mok on charges of accepting bribery.
- As South Korea's trade deficit worsens, on February 15 the government will begin active measures to support exports by increasing loans to exporting companies.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday said the United States will continue to be involved in peace talks between the two Koreas, and asked Congress to continue funding of an agreement to dismantle North Korea's nuclear weapons programme.
- With the dollar's strength continuing against the won, private citizens and small- and medium-sized companies are also attempting to accumulate the U.S. currency.
